ordered_diagnoses: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms

s1.syndrome_frame: Severe cutaneous adverse reaction to immunotherapy
salient_findings: Severely pruritic, nontender, erythematous papular and macular eruption
Rash progression despite initial treatment with hydrocortisone and diphenhydramine
Rash reached grade III severity with worsening pruritus
key_facts: 54-year-old man with glioblastoma
Treated with M7824, a bifunctional fusion protein targeting PD-L1 and TGF-β
Rash appeared four weeks after initiation of M7824
No other new medications were being taken
Initial classification of the eruption as a grade I rash
Rash and pruritus progressed despite treatment with hydrocortisone and diphenhydramine
Doxycycline was started for a suspected acneiform eruption
Laboratory evaluation showed no elevations in liver enzymes, no eosinophilia, and no lymphadenopathy
Treatment with triamcinolone and hydroxyzine did not improve symptoms
M7824 infusions were held, and prednisone was initiated at 40 mg per day

shortlist: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Severe cutaneous adverse reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced a severe, pruritic, erythematous papular and macular eruption after initiation of M7824, consistent with a severe cutaneous adverse reaction to immunotherapy.

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's rash progressed to grade III with worsening pruritus, despite treatment, which is consistent with the severe skin detachment and mucous membrane involvement seen in Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

shortlist.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's rash was severe and progressive, with a high grade of severity, which is consistent with the extensive skin detachment and necrosis seen in toxic epidermal necrolysis.

shortlist.label: Maculopapular drug eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed a maculopapular rash after initiation of M7824, which is a common type of drug eruption.

shortlist.label: PD-1 inhibitor-associated rash
shortlist.why_kept: M7824 targets PD-L1, and the patient developed a rash, which is consistent with the immune-mediated cutaneous adverse reactions seen with PD-1 inhibitors.

shortlist.label: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
shortlist.why_kept: Although the patient did not have eosinophilia, the rash was severe and progressive, and the patient had systemic symptoms, such as pruritus, which is consistent with this diagnosis.

shortlist.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed a widespread, erythematous, papular and macular eruption, which is consistent with the clinical presentation of acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis.

shortlist.label: Immune-mediated cutaneous adverse reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed a severe cutaneous adverse reaction after initiation of M7824, which is an immune-mediated therapy, consistent with an immune-mediated cutaneous adverse reaction.

raw.rationale: The patient developed a pruritic, erythematous papular and macular eruption after starting M7824, with no other new medications, and laboratory evaluation showed no elevations in liver enzymes, no eosinophilia, and no lymphadenopathy, consistent with a maculopapular drug eruption.

rejected.label: Severe cutaneous adverse reaction
rejected.why: Too broad, as it encompasses several severe skin reactions, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, which are not supported by the presence of necrosis or epidermal detachment in the vignette

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
rejected.why: Not supported by the vignette, as there is no mention of mucosal involvement or epidermal necrosis

rejected.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
rejected.why: Not supported by the vignette, as there is no mention of widespread epidermal necrosis or detachment

rejected.label: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
rejected.why: Not supported by the vignette, as laboratory evaluation showed no eosinophilia

rejected.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
rejected.why: Not supported by the vignette, as the eruption is described as papular and macular, without pustules

rejected.label: Immune-mediated cutaneous adverse reaction
rejected.why: Too broad, as it encompasses several types of skin reactions, including the champion diagnosis

rejected.label: PD-1 inhibitor-associated rash
rejected.why: While M7824 targets PD-L1, the presentation is more consistent with a maculopapular drug eruption, which can occur with various medications, including PD-1 inhibitors
